citation: Amorim AAPO, Oliveira MG, Mancini MC, Sirqueira AS (2021) "Rheological, EMI and corrosion properties of epoxy coating with nanoparticle and conductive carbon black", SN Applied Sciences 3:236.

in_scope_rationale: Bi-component commercial DGEBA epoxy resin / polyamide (amine-class) hardener anti-corrosion coating (grade JUMBO, volume solids 80%, TiO2 filler 25%, general filler 32%) applied to steel substrates and evaluated for 3.5wt% NaCl corrosion resistance -- squarely in the marine/industrial anti-corrosion two-part epoxy-amine coating scope. Modification is with conductive carbon black + organoclay nanoparticles (APA, HT), not pigment PVC, so this closes HERSCHEL_BULKLEY only, not KRIEGER_DOUGHERTY (no pigment/filler volume-fraction viscosity ladder in this source).
table_transcribed: Table 2a (Herschel-Bulkley fitted rheological parameters), from steady-shear flow curves measured on a stress-controlled rheometer (parallel plates, 40mm, 25C, 1mm gap, shear rate 0.1 to 100 /s), fit with R software per the paper's Methods 2.3. Model: eta = tau_0/gamma_dot + K*gamma_dot^(n-1) (paper's Eq.1), which is byte-identical in functional form to amphora-viscosity-score::herschel_bulkley_apparent_viscosity (src/lib.rs:1227): yield_stress_pa/shear_rate_s_inv + consistency_pa_s_n*shear_rate_s_inv.powf(flow_index_n - 1.0).
data_integrity_note: IMPORTANT -- the as-printed PDF table renders tau_0 and K with a comma before the final 3 digits for every one of the 12 values in this sub-table (e.g. '123,900', '1,054,000'), while n, R-squared and MRD% in the SAME table use a period as decimal point (e.g. '0.7069', '0.9995'). This is internally inconsistent formatting (locale decimal-mark mixup, most likely introduced by a Word/Excel-to-PDF export on a machine with Brazilian pt-BR locale defaults, given the authors' Brazilian affiliations). Reading tau_0/K literally as English thousands-grouped integers (e.g. tau_0_epoxy = 123900 Pa) is numerically INCONSISTENT with the paper's own Fig.3 apparent-viscosity axis (explicitly bounded 1e0 to 1e5 Pa.s over the same 0.1-100 /s shear-rate range): plugging the literal reading into the paper's own Eq.1 at gamma_dot=0.1/s yields eta_apparent = 1.34e6 Pa.s for the Epoxy control alone (13x the chart's own axis ceiling), and every other formulation's literal tau_0 is even larger. The internally-consistent reading (last comma = decimal separator, matching every other decimal field in the table) divides tau_0 and K by 1000; plugging THAT reading into the same equation reproduces the paper's stated Fig.3 axis range (1e0-1e5 Pa.s) for all 6 formulations at both shear-rate extremes -- this is the value used as 'corrected' below, and it is what this benchmark tests the module against. Both readings are recorded raw below for auditability.
